claims.evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data identifying 81 differentially expressed transcripts and 56 differentially expressed genes (Figure 5).

claims.claim: Rbfox2-TGF-β-Tak1 signaling axis is deregulated by Rbfox2 deletion.
claims.source: We demonstrate that Rbfox2-TGF-β-Tak1 signaling axis is deregulated by Rbfox2 deletion.
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced Tak1, pTak1, pSmad2-C, and p-p38 Mapk levels in Rbfox2 mutants (Figure 6A, D).

claims.claim: Restoration of TGF-β signaling by Tak1 overexpression can rescue the proliferation defect seen in Rbfox2 mutants.
claims.source: Furthermore, restoration of TGF-β signaling by Tak1 overexpression can rescue the proliferation defect seen in Rbfox2 mutants.
claims.evidence: Supported by Ki67 immunostaining data showing increased proliferation in Rbfox2 mutant cells after Tak1 overexpression (Figure 6F-H).

claims.claim: TGF-β signaling promotes expression of Rbfox2 in NCCs through a positive feedback loop.
claims.source: We also identified a positive feedback loop in which TGF-β signaling promotes expression of Rbfox2 in NCCs.
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing increased Rbfox2 expression after TGF-β stimulation (Figure 7A) and luciferase assays showing Smad-dependent activation of Rbfox2 promoter (Figure 7E-G).

claims.claim: At E9.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in the premigratory NCCs at the dorsal neural tube, as well as in the migratory NCCs throughout the rostrocaudal axis.
claims.source: At E9.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in the premigratory NCCs at the dorsal neural tube, as well as in the migratory NCCs (Figure 1A–C,F–H,K–M) throughout the rostrocaudal axis, with strong expression of Rbfox2 observed in the somites.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Rbfox2 expression pattern at E9.5 (Figure 1A-C, F-H, K-M).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 expression is observed with strong expression in the somites at E9.5.
claims.source: At E9.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in the premigratory NCCs at the dorsal neural tube, as well as in the migratory NCCs (Figure 1A–C,F–H,K–M) throughout the rostrocaudal axis, with strong expression of Rbfox2 observed in the somites.
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Rbfox2 expression in somites (Figure 1).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 expression is gradually reduced in migratory NCCs.
claims.source: Rbfox2 expression is gradually reduced in migratory NCCs (Figure 1K–M).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing reduced Rbfox2 expression in migratory NCCs (Figure 1K-M).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 expression was detected in the neural crest-derived craniofacial tissues including the palate shelves.
claims.source: Rbfox2 expression was detected in the neural crest-derived craniofacial tissues including the palate shelves but not in the cardiac tissues such as OFT (Figure 1D–E,I–J,N–O).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Rbfox2 expression in palate shelves (Figure 1D-E, I-J, N-O).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 expression was not detected in the cardiac tissues such as OFT.
claims.source: Rbfox2 expression was detected in the neural crest-derived craniofacial tissues including the palate shelves but not in the cardiac tissues such as OFT (Figure 1D–E,I–J,N–O).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing absence of Rbfox2 expression in OFT (Figure 1D-E, I-J, N-O).

claims.claim: At E9.5, Rbfox2 expression is identical to Pax3 in NCCs, dorsal neural tube, and somites.
claims.source: At E9.5, Rbfox2 expression is identical to Pax3 in NCCs, dorsal neural tube, and somites (Figure 1P and S).
claims.evidence: Supported by comparative immunostaining images of Rbfox2 and Pax3 at E9.5 (Figure 1P, S).

claims.claim: At E10.5, in addition to premigratory NCCs, Rbfox2 is also expressed in the dorsal root ganglia.
claims.source: At E10.5, in addition to premigratory NCCs, Rbfox2 is also expressed in the dorsal root ganglia (Figure 1Q).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Rbfox2 expression in dorsal root ganglia at E10.5 (Figure 1Q).

claims.claim: At E10.5, in contrast to Pax3 expression in the dorsal neural tube, the Rbfox2 expression is more restricted to the ventral neural tube.
claims.source: In contrast to Pax3 expression in the dorsal neural tube, the Rbfox2 expression is more restricted to the ventral neural tube (Figure 1Q and T).
claims.evidence: Supported by comparative immunostaining images showing different expression patterns of Rbfox2 and Pax3 in neural tube at E10.5 (Figure 1Q, T).

claims.claim: At E11.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in the ventral neural tube and dorsal root ganglia.
claims.source: At E11.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in the ventral neural tube and dorsal root ganglia (Figure 1R).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Rbfox2 expression pattern at E11.5 (Figure 1R).

claims.claim: At E11.5, Pax3 is more restricted to the dorsal neural tube.
claims.source: However, Pax3 is more restricted to the dorsal neural tube (Figure 1U).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining images showing Pax3 expression pattern at E11.5 (Figure 1U).

claims.claim: Pax3Cre/+-mediated deletion of Rbfox2 results in neonatal lethality.
claims.source: We observed that Pax3Cre/+-mediated deletion of Rbfox2 results in neonatal lethality.
claims.evidence: Supported by genotyping data showing no mutant pups recovered at postnatal day 10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos develop a cleft palate and defects in the development of craniofacial skeleton.
claims.source: Rbfox2 mutant (Rbfox2Pax3-CKO) embryos develop a cleft palate and defects in the development of craniofacial skeleton, suggesting defective cranial neural crest development.
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological data showing cleft palate and craniofacial defects (Figure 2, Figure 4).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO mutants developed a cleft palate and craniofacial skeleton defects and died postnatally at day 1.
claims.source: Similar to Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO mutants developed a cleft palate and craniofacial skeleton defects and died postnatally at day 1.
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological data showing cleft palate and craniofacial defects in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos (Figure 2M-T, Figure 4L-S).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos are present at the expected Mendelian ratios at all embryonic time points analyzed (E10.5-E18.5).
claims.source: Genotyping of embryos from series of timed point matings demonstrated that Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos are present at the expected Mendelian ratios at all embryonic time points analyzed (E10.5-E18.5) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by genotyping data showing expected Mendelian ratios at embryonic stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Pax3-CKO mutant pups die at postnatal day one (P1).
claims.source: However, pups monitoring after birth revealed that mutant pups that are characterized by a shortened body axis and abnormal craniofacial features die at postnatal day one (P1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and G).
claims.evidence: Supported by genotyping data showing no mutant pups at P10 and morphological data at P1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B, G).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos develop severe subcutaneous edema in mid- and late-gestation.
claims.source: Our morphological and histological analyses demonstrate that Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos develop cleft palate and severe subcutaneous edema, which are present in mid- and late-gestation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–F,H–K).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing edema in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-F, H-K).

claims.claim: The neonatal lethality in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO pups is caused by respiratory failure.
claims.source: Irregular breathing and hardly inflated lungs in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO pups support the notion that the neonatal lethality is caused by respiratory failure (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L–O).
claims.evidence: Supported by histological images showing uninflated lungs in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO pups (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L-O).

claims.claim: In Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, development of primary palates is not affected.
claims.source: In Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, development of primary palates is not affected.
claims.evidence: Stated in text without specific figure reference, but consistent with focus on secondary palate defects.

claims.claim: All of the Rbfox2Pax3-CKO pups died neonatally, exhibiting a secondary cleft palate defect.
claims.source: However, all of the Rbfox2Pax3-CKO pups died neonatally, exhibiting a secondary cleft palate defect.
claims.evidence: Supported by genotyping data showing no mutant pups at P10 and morphological data showing cleft palate (Figure 2).

claims.claim: At E12.5, the palatal shelves in both control and Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos were initiated normally, growing vertically flanking the developing tongue.
claims.source: At E12.5, the palatal shelves in both control and Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos were initiated normally, growing vertically flanking the developing tongue (Figure 2A–B,G–H).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing normal palatal shelf orientation at E12.5 (Figure 2A-B, G-H).

claims.claim: No obvious morphological or histological differences were observed between control and Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos at E12.5.
claims.source: No obvious morphological or histological differences were observed at this embryonic stage.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing E12.5 palatal shelves, supported by Figure 2A-B, G-H.

claims.claim: At E15.5 and E18.5, the control palatal shelves were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position and met each other at the midline along the anterior-posterior axis.
claims.source: At E15.5 and E18.5, the control palatal shelves were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position and met each other at the midline along the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2C–F).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing normal palate fusion in controls (Figure 2C-F).

claims.claim: In Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, palatal shelves were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position, but they completely failed to fuse at the midline throughout the anterior-posterior axis.
claims.source: However, in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, palatal shelves were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position, but they completely failed to fuse at the midline throughout the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2I–L).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing cleft palate in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos (Figure 2I-L).

claims.claim: Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio but died at P1.
claims.source: Similar to Rbfox2Pax3-CKO, Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio but died at P1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1P–R).
claims.evidence: Supported by genotyping data showing expected Mendelian ratios at embryonic stages but no mutants at P10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1P).

claims.claim: In Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos, palatal shelves were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position, but completely failed to fuse at the midline throughout the anterior-posterior axis.
claims.source: Similar to Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos, palatal shelves in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos were elevated above the tongue to a horizontal position, but completely failed to fuse at the midline throughout the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 2M–T).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing cleft palate in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos (Figure 2M-T).

claims.claim: Ki67 immunohistochemistry revealed a significant reduction in cell proliferation in Rbfox2 mutants when compared with control embryos at E12.5.
claims.source: Ki67 immunohistochemistry revealed a significant reduction in cell proliferation in Rbfox2 mutants when compared with control embryos at E12.5, in which the morphological or histological changes were not evident (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: Supported by Ki67 immunostaining and quantification showing reduced proliferation at E12.5 (Figure 3A-C).

claims.claim: A significant difference in cell proliferation was more evident at E15.5 in Rbfox2 mutants compared to controls.
claims.source: A significant difference in cell proliferation was more evident at E15.5 (Figure 3D–F and G–I).
claims.evidence: Supported by Ki67 immunostaining and quantification showing reduced proliferation at E15.5 (Figure 3D-F, G-I).

claims.claim: TUNEL assay demonstrated no differences in cell death between the control and Rbfox2 mutants at E15.5.
claims.source: TUNEL assay demonstrated no differences in cell death between the control and Rbfox2 mutants at E15.5 (Figure 3J–K).
claims.evidence: Supported by TUNEL assay images showing similar apoptosis levels (Figure 3J-K).

claims.claim: E-cadherin expression is observed in the nasal, palatal and tongue epithelium and not affected by Rbfox2 deletion.
claims.source: E-cadherin expression is observed in the nasal, palatal and tongue epithelium and not affected by Rbfox2 deletion (Figure 3L–M).
claims.evidence: Supported by E-cadherin immunostaining images showing similar expression patterns in control and mutant (Figure 3L-M).

claims.claim: Labeled neural crest cells marked by GFP immunostaining were abundantly present in the palate shelves of mutant embryos at E15.5.
claims.source: Labeled neural crest cells marked by GFP immunostaining were abundantly present in the palate shelves of mutant embryos (Figure 3N–O).
claims.evidence: Supported by GFP immunostaining images showing neural crest-derived cells in mutant palate shelves (Figure 3N-O).

claims.claim: No obvious NCCs migration defect was observed in Rbfox2 mutant embryos at E12.5 and E14.5.
claims.source: No obvious NCCs migration defect was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by lineage-tracing images showing similar NCC distribution in control and mutant embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: In both Rbfox2Pax3-CKO and Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos, neural crest-derived frontal bones of the calvaria were hypoplastic and widely separated leaving a wide dorsal opening.
claims.source: In both Rbfox2Pax3-CKO and Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos, neural crest-derived bones such as frontal bones of the calvaria were hypoplastic and widely separated leaving a wide dorsal opening (Figure 4C and M).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing hypoplastic frontal bones (Figure 4C, M).

claims.claim: Decreased ossification of nasal bone was observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO mutant embryos compared to the controls.
claims.source: Decreased ossification of nasal bone was observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO mutant embryos compared to the controls (Figure 4B–C and L–M).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing reduced nasal bone ossification (Figure 4B-C, L-M).

claims.claim: Reduction in the lower jaw or mandible size was observed in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Reduction in the lower jaw or mandible size was observed in Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4E–H and N–Q).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing smaller mandible (Figure 4E-H, N-Q).

claims.claim: Both the shape and size of most neural crest-derived bones including alisphenoid, premaxilla, palatal process of premaxilla, palatal process of maxilla and palatine are affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Further analysis revealed that both the shape and size of most neural crest-derived bones including alisphenoid, premaxilla, palatal process of premaxilla, palatal process of maxilla and palatine are affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4J–K and R–S).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing malformed craniofacial bones (Figure 4J-K, R-S).

claims.claim: The palatal process of palatine bone is missing in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: The palatal process of palatine bone is also missing in Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4K and S).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing absence of palatal process of palatine bone (Figure 4K, S).

claims.claim: Ectopic bone formation and fusion of vertebral bodies were observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: Ectopic bone formation and fusion of vertebral bodies were observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing vertebral defects (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: No defects in the axial skeletons were observed in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos.
claims.source: No defects in the axial skeletons were observed in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by skeletal staining images showing normal axial skeleton in Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).

claims.claim: Reduced thickness in the ossified calvaria bone was observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: Von Kossa staining of the calvaria from E17.5 Rbfox2Pax3-CKO mutant embryos revealed the impaired development of mesenchymal condensations that become ossified bone (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). Reduced thickness in the ossified calvaria bone was observed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.evidence: Supported by Von Kossa staining images showing reduced bone thickness (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).

claims.claim: The development of cardiac OFT was not affected in Rbfox2 mutants.
claims.source: As shown by normal septation and alignment of the aorta and pulmonary trunk, the development of cardiac OFT was not affected in Rbfox2 mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–J).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing normal OFT development (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-J).

claims.claim: Cardiac NCCs migration was grossly intact in the Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Fate-mapping analysis demonstrated that cardiac NCCs migration was grossly intact in the Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K–P).
claims.evidence: Supported by fate-mapping images showing normal cardiac NCC distribution (Figure 4—figure supplement 2K-P).

claims.claim: The neurofilament 2H3 staining in Rbfox2 mutant embryos revealed abnormalities in the oculomotor (III), trochlear (IV) and hypoglossal nerve (XII cranial nerve).
claims.source: The neurofilament 2H3 staining in Rbfox2 mutant embryos revealed abnormalities in the oculomotor (III), trochlear (IV) and hypoglossal nerve (XII cranial nerve) (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: Supported by whole mount neurofilament staining images showing cranial nerve defects (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).

claims.claim: Oculomotor and trochlear nerves appear to be deformed in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: Oculomotor and trochlear nerves appear to be deformed.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing cranial nerve analysis, supported by Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: The hypoglossal cranial nerve is disorganized and shorter in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: The hypoglossal cranial nerve is disorganized and shorter in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: Supported by whole mount neurofilament staining images showing hypoglossal nerve defects (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).

claims.claim: No significant difference was observed in the size of the dorsal root ganglion between control and Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: No significant difference was observed in the size of the dorsal root ganglion (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: Supported by quantification of dorsal root ganglia size (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).

claims.claim: Enteric nervous system development was not affected in the absence of Rbfox2.
claims.source: Enteric nervous system development was not affected in the absence of Rbfox2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C–D).
claims.evidence: Supported by whole mount neurofilament staining and lineage tracing images showing normal enteric nervous system (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C-D).

claims.claim: Thymus was not affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Similarly, other neural crest-derived organs such as thymus and adrenal gland (chromaffin cells) were not affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 4, and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological and histological images showing normal thymus development (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).

claims.claim: Adrenal gland (chromaffin cells) was not affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Similarly, other neural crest-derived organs such as thymus and adrenal gland (chromaffin cells) were not affected in Rbfox2 mutant embryos (Figure 4—figure supplement 4, and Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
claims.evidence: Supported by morphological, histological, and immunostaining images showing normal adrenal gland development (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).

claims.claim: No significant changes were found in limb and diaphragm muscles in Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos.
claims.source: Since Pax3Cre/+ transgene is active in non-neural crest-derived tissues such as limb and diaphragm muscles, we also analyzed these tissues and found no significant changes (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
claims.evidence: Supported by histological images showing normal muscle development (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).

claims.claim: Using MISO analysis, 81 differentially expressed transcripts from 59 genes were identified in Rbfox2 mutant samples as compared with control.
claims.source: Using MISO analysis, we identified 81 differentially expressed transcripts from 59 genes in Rbfox2 mutant samples as compared with control (Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data analysis using MISO (Figure 5B).

claims.claim: Cuffdiff analysis identified 33 alternatively spliced transcripts from 30 genes in Rbfox2 mutant samples as compared with controls.
claims.source: However, Cuffdiff analysis identified 33 alternatively spliced transcripts from 30 genes in Rbfox2 mutant samples as compared with controls (Figure 5C and Figure 5—source data 2).
claims.evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data analysis using Cuffdiff (Figure 5C).

claims.claim: Pathway enrichment analysis identified significant enrichment of genes that control cellular and anatomical structure morphogenesis.
claims.source: Pathway enrichment analysis identified significant enrichment of genes that control cellular and anatomical structure morphogenesis (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Supported by pathway enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data (Figure 5D).

claims.claim: Significant UGCAUG motif enrichment was identified only in the introns of the Rbfox2 target genes (adjusted p-value=1.4E-08).
claims.source: We performed an analysis of motif enrichment (AME) through the MEME suite (version 5.0.5) and identified significant UGCAUG motif enrichment only in the introns of the Rbfox2 target genes (adjusted p-value=1.4E-08) (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Supported by motif enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data (Figure 5E).

claims.claim: Most UGCAUG sequences were located within 1000 bases of the exon on either flanking introns in Rbfox2 target genes.
claims.source: Most UGCAUG sequences were located within 1000 bases of the exon on either flanking introns (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: Supported by FIMO analysis showing location of UGCAUG sequences (Figure 5F).

claims.claim: Venn analysis identified 11 transcripts that were identified by both MISO and Cuffdiff programs.
claims.source: Venn analysis identified 11 transcripts that were identified by both programs and constituted a high confidence set of differentially expressed and AS isoforms in Rbfox2 mutants (Figure 5G–H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by Venn diagram analysis of RNA-Seq data (Figure 5G-H).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 deletion significantly impacted splicing and expression of Map3k7, Fn1, Postn and Uap1.
claims.source: Using RNA isolated from control and Rbfox2 knockout craniofacial tissues, we validated the splicing changes identified by RNA-Seq by performing reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR) in a selected group of genes such as mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 7 (Map3k7), fibronectin 1 (Fn1), periostin (Postn) and UAP1 UDP-N-acetylglucosamine pyrophosphorylase 1 (Uap1). Rbfox2 deletion significantly impacted splicing and expression of these candidate genes (Figure 5I–L).
claims.evidence: Supported by RT-PCR validation and qRT-PCR data (Figure 5I-L).

claims.claim: Rbfox2 deletion reduced the expression of the predominantly expressed Map3k7 transcript.
claims.source: For example, Rbfox2 deletion reduced the expression of the predominantly expressed Map3k7 transcript.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing RT-PCR validation results, supported by Figure 5I, L.

claims.claim: The short Fn1 transcript was not present in Rbfox2 mutants.
claims.source: The short Fn1 transcript was not present in Rbfox2 mutants.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing RT-PCR validation results, supported by Figure 5I.

claims.claim: Rbfox2 can directly bind to the RNA of Map3k7, Fn1, Postn and Uap1 target genes and modulate splicing.
claims.source: To determine that Rbfox2 directly bind to these target genes in vivo, we performed RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) assays using anti-Rbfox2 antibody on palatal mesenchymal cells, followed by quantitative RT-PCR. We observed significant enrichment suggesting that Rbfox2 can directly bind to the RNA of these target genes and modulate splicing (Figure 5J).
claims.evidence: Supported by RNA-IP assay data showing enrichment of target transcripts (Figure 5J).

claims.claim: 56 differentially expressed genes were identified between control and Rbfox2 knockouts.
claims.source: To determine the transcriptional changes associated with the craniofacial defects, we analyzed genes that are differentially expressed between control and Rbfox2 knockouts. We identified 56 differentially expressed genes (Figure 5K).
claims.evidence: Supported by RNA-Seq data analysis showing differentially expressed genes (Figure 5K).

claims.claim: A significant reduction in Map3k7, Fn1, Myl1, Sfrs18 and Smarca2 was observed in Rbfox2 knockout tissues.
claims.source: We observed a significant reduction in Map3k7, Fn1, Myl1, Sfrs18 and Smarca2 in Rbfox2 knockout tissues (Figure 5L).
claims.evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR validation data (Figure 5L).

claims.claim: Both Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1 levels were significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: To identify if TGF-β signaling pathway is affected by Rbfox2 deletion in vivo, we harvested palatal shelves from control and Rbfox2 mutant embryos and performed western blot analysis for Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1. We found that both Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1 levels were significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant embryos, demonstrating impaired TGF-β signaling pathway in neural crest-derived palate shelves (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced Tak1 and pTak1 levels (Figure 6A).

claims.claim: The level of C-terminal Smad2 phosphorylation was significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: The level of C-terminal Smad2 phosphorylation was significantly reduced; however, no change in total Smad2 was observed.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing western blot results, supported by Figure 6A.

claims.claim: No change in total Smad2 was observed in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: The level of C-terminal Smad2 phosphorylation was significantly reduced; however, no change in total Smad2 was observed.
claims.evidence: Stated in text describing western blot results, supported by Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The level of phosphorylated p38 Mapk was significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Similarly, the level of phosphorylated p38 Mapk was significantly reduced, although there was no change in total p38 Mapk (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced p-p38 Mapk levels (Figure 6A).

claims.claim: No change in total p38 Mapk was observed in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
claims.source: Similarly, the level of phosphorylated p38 Mapk was significantly reduced, although there was no change in total p38 Mapk (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing similar total p38 Mapk levels (Figure 6A).

claims.claim: Fn1 protein levels were significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant neural crest as compared with controls.
claims.source: Consistent with the reduction in its mRNA levels, Fn1 protein levels were also significantly reduced in Rbfox2 mutant neural crest as compared with controls (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data showing reduced Fn1 protein levels (Figure 6B).

claims.claim: Majority of the cultured palatal mesenchymal cells were GFP positive confirming their neural crest origin.
claims.source: The neural crest cell's origin and purity were confirmed by growing cultures of Pax3Cre/+;Rbfox2flox/+;Rosa26mTmG/+ embryos. Majority of the cultured cells were GFP positive confirming their neural crest origin (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by fluorescent images showing GFP-positive cultured cells (Figure 6C).

claims.claim: Palatal mesenchymal cells isolated from Rbfox2 mutant embryos showed reduced levels of both Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1 when compared with control following TGF-β stimulation.
claims.source: Consistent with the in vivo data, palatal mesenchymal cells isolated from Rbfox2 mutant embryos showed reduced levels of both Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1 when compared with control following TGF-β stimulation (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data from TGF-β stimulated cultured cells (Figure 6D).

claims.claim: No significant change in pTak1/Tak1 ratio was observed in Rbfox2 mutant cells, suggesting that Tak1 activation was not affected by Rbfox2 deletion.
claims.source: In addition, no significant change in pTak1/Tak1 ratio was observed, suggesting that Tak1 activation was not affected by Rbfox2 deletion (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: Supported by quantification of western blot data showing similar pTak1/Tak1 ratio (Figure 6E).

claims.claim: TGF-β-induced C-terminal Smad2 phosphorylation levels were reduced in Rbfox2 mutant cells when compared with controls.
claims.source: Similarly, TGF-β-induced C-terminal Smad2 and p38 Mapk phosphorylation levels were reduced in Rbfox2 mutant cells when compared with controls, while no significant change was observed in total Smad2 or p38 Mapk (Figure 6D–E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by western blot data from TGF-β stimulated cultured cells (Figure 6D-E).

claims.claim: TGF-β-induced p38 Mapk phosphorylation levels were reduced in Rbfox2 mutant cells when compared with controls.

results.result: Rbfox2 is expressed in neural crest cells (NCCs) during mouse embryogenesis. At E9.5, Rbfox2 is expressed in premigratory and migratory NCCs throughout the rostrocaudal axis, with strong expression in somites. Expression is detected in neural crest-derived craniofacial tissues including palate shelves but not in cardiac tissues such as OFT. Rbfox2 expression pattern changes from E9.5 to E11.5, with expression becoming more restricted to ventral neural tube at later stages.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C8-C17 are well-supported by immunostaining data showing Rbfox2 expression patterns at multiple embryonic stages (E9.5-E11.5) in various tissues. The spatial and temporal expression patterns are documented with appropriate controls (Pax3 comparison) and multiple tissue sections. The data consistently demonstrate Rbfox2 expression in NCCs and neural crest-derived tissues.

results.result: Neural crest-specific deletion of Rbfox2 using either Pax3Cre or Wnt1Cre results in neonatal lethality with cleft palate and craniofacial bone defects. Rbfox2 mutant embryos are present at expected Mendelian ratios during embryonic development but die at postnatal day 1. At E12.5, palatal shelves develop normally, but by E15.5-E18.5, palatal shelves fail to fuse at the midline despite proper elevation. Neonatal lethality is attributed to respiratory failure.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C3, C18-C32 are strongly supported by comprehensive morphological, histological, and genotyping data from two independent Cre lines (Pax3Cre and Wnt1Cre). The temporal analysis of palate development shows consistent phenotypes across both mutant lines. The respiratory failure conclusion (C24) is supported by lung histology showing uninflated lungs, though direct functional measurements are not provided.

results.result: Rbfox2 deletion causes reduced cell proliferation in palatal shelves at E12.5 and E15.5 without affecting cell death, E-cadherin expression, or neural crest cell migration. Neural crest-derived cells are present in mutant palate shelves, indicating that the cleft palate defect is not due to impaired NCC migration.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C38 are supported by Ki67 immunostaining showing reduced proliferation, TUNEL assays showing no change in apoptosis, E-cadherin staining showing normal epithelial marker expression, and lineage tracing showing presence of NCCs in palate shelves. The data provide converging evidence that the palate defect is primarily due to reduced proliferation rather than cell death or migration defects.

results.result: Rbfox2 deletion causes severe craniofacial skeletal defects including hypoplastic frontal bones, decreased nasal bone ossification, reduced mandible size, and malformed neural crest-derived bones. The palatal process of palatine bone is missing in mutants. Rbfox2Pax3-CKO embryos also show axial skeletal defects including ectopic bone formation and vertebral fusion, while Rbfox2Wnt1-CKO embryos have normal axial skeletons.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C46 are well-supported by skeletal staining (Alizarin Red/Alcian Blue) and Von Kossa staining showing consistent craniofacial bone defects in both Pax3-CKO and Wnt1-CKO mutants. The difference in axial skeletal phenotypes between the two Cre lines (C44 vs C45) is expected given that Pax3Cre is active in somites while Wnt1Cre is neural crest-specific, providing internal validation of the experimental approach.

results.result: Rbfox2 deletion does not affect cardiac OFT development, cardiac NCC migration, dorsal root ganglia size, enteric nervous system, thymus, adrenal gland chromaffin cells, or limb and diaphragm muscles. However, abnormalities are observed in cranial nerves (oculomotor, trochlear, and hypoglossal).
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C56 are supported by morphological, histological, immunostaining, and lineage tracing data showing normal development of most neural crest-derived and Pax3-expressing tissues. The cranial nerve defects (C49-C51) are documented by neurofilament staining. The selective tissue-specific effects correlate with Rbfox2 expression patterns (absent in OFT, C12), providing internal consistency.

results.result: RNA-Seq analysis reveals that Rbfox2 regulates splicing and expression of numerous genes essential for neural crest/craniofacial development. MISO identified 81 differentially expressed transcripts from 59 genes, while Cuffdiff identified 33 alternatively spliced transcripts from 30 genes. Pathway enrichment shows genes controlling cellular and anatomical structure morphogenesis. UGCAUG motif enrichment is significant in introns of Rbfox2 target genes. Validated targets include Map3k7, Fn1, Postn, and Uap1, with Rbfox2 directly binding to their RNA. 56 differentially expressed genes were identified, including reduced expression of Map3k7, Fn1, Myl1, Sfrs18, and Smarca2.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C57-C68 are well-supported by comprehensive RNA-Seq analysis with appropriate bioinformatic approaches (MISO and Cuffdiff), validation by RT-PCR and qRT-PCR, RNA-IP demonstrating direct binding, and motif enrichment analysis. The use of E12.5 tissue (before major morphological changes) is appropriate for identifying primary molecular changes. The convergence of two independent analysis methods (MISO and Cuffdiff) identifying 11 common transcripts (C62) provides high-confidence targets.

results.result: The Rbfox2-TGFβ-Tak1 signaling axis is deregulated in Rbfox2 mutants. Both Tak1 and phosphorylated Tak1 levels are significantly reduced in vivo and in cultured palatal mesenchymal cells. Downstream signaling shows reduced phosphorylation of Smad2-C and p38 Mapk without changes in total protein levels. Fn1 protein levels are also reduced. The pTak1/Tak1 ratio is unchanged, suggesting Tak1 activation is not affected.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C69-C82 are strongly supported by western blot data from both in vivo tissue and cultured cells, with quantification showing consistent reductions in Tak1 expression and downstream signaling. The observation that pTak1/Tak1 ratio is unchanged (C77) indicates the defect is at the level of Tak1 expression rather than activation, which is consistent with the RNA-Seq data showing reduced Map3k7 expression. The use of both in vivo and in vitro systems strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: Restoration of TGFβ signaling by Tak1 overexpression rescues the proliferation defect in Rbfox2 mutant palatal mesenchymal cells. Cultured palatal mesenchymal cells are confirmed to be of neural crest origin (GFP positive). Rbfox2 mutant cells proliferate slower than controls, and Tak1 overexpression increases both Tak1 and pTak1 levels and rescues proliferation. Tak1 overexpression also increases Map3k7 and Fn1 expression but not Myl1, Sfrs18, or Smarca2.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C75, C83-C87 are supported by Ki67 proliferation assays, western blots confirming Tak1 overexpression, and qRT-PCR showing selective gene expression changes. The rescue experiment provides functional evidence that Tak1 acts downstream of Rbfox2. The selective rescue of Map3k7 and Fn1 but not other genes (C86-C87) suggests specificity in the Tak1-mediated pathway. The confirmation of neural crest origin of cultured cells (C75) validates the cell culture model.

results.result: TGFβ signaling promotes Rbfox2 expression through a positive feedback loop. TGFβ treatment increases Rbfox2 expression in wildtype palatal mesenchymal cells. Smad3 and Tak1 inhibitors abolish TGFβ-induced Rbfox2 expression, while p38 inhibitor has no effect. Two sites with multiple Smad binding elements (SBEs) were identified in the Rbfox2 promoter. Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4 activate the Rbfox2 luciferase reporter, with higher activation in the presence of TGFβ. ChIP assays demonstrate that Smad2/3 binds directly to SBEs in the Rbfox2 promoter in vivo, with enrichment after TGFβ treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C88-C98 are well-supported by multiple complementary approaches: western blots showing TGFβ-induced Rbfox2 expression, pharmacological inhibitor studies defining pathway components, promoter analysis identifying SBEs, luciferase reporter assays demonstrating functional activation, and ChIP assays confirming direct Smad2/3 binding. The convergence of these independent methods provides strong evidence for the positive feedback loop. The differential effects of inhibitors (Smad3 and Tak1 but not p38) help define the pathway mechanism.

results.result: The striking similarities in craniofacial and skeletal phenotypes between Tak1 and Rbfox2 mutants suggest that Tak1 is a downstream target of Rbfox2 and may significantly contribute to the phenotype. Tak1 regulates neural crest-derived tissues downstream of Rbfox2.
results.evaluation: Claims C152-C154 are supported by the phenotypic similarities between Rbfox2 and previously published Tak1 mutants, the RNA-Seq data showing reduced Map3k7 expression, the western blot data showing reduced Tak1 protein, and the rescue experiments showing that Tak1 overexpression restores proliferation. While the claims are somewhat inferential, they are well-supported by the convergence of genetic, molecular, and functional data.

results.result: Other Rbfox2 target genes identified in the RNA-Seq screen may be responsible or contribute to the craniofacial phenotype present in Rbfox2 mutant embryos.
results.evaluation: Claim C155 is speculative and acknowledged as such by the authors. While the RNA-Seq data identify numerous potential target genes, functional validation is limited to a few genes (Map3k7, Fn1, Postn, Uap1). The contribution of other target genes to the phenotype remains to be determined and would require additional functional studies.
